nodes.title: Irreducibility and eigenvalue lemmas in characteristic p
nodes.statement: (Lemmas 6.1–6.5.) Let A ≅ k[[λ]] with fraction field K and ρ : G_Σ → GL₂(A) with (6.2): ρ ⊗ K̄ irreducible and of type A, B or unramified at each w ∤ p; ρ mod λ = ρ_c; Σ ⊇ primes above p and where ρ̄ ramifies; ρ of type A or B exactly where ρ̄ is; det ρ = χ; ρ|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_1 *; 0 χ_2) with χ_1/χ_2 of infinite order for each v | p. Then W = ad⁰ρ ⊗ K̄ is irreducible (ρ ⊗ K̄ not dihedral); ρ ⊗ K̄|_{Gal(F_Σ/F⁺)} is neither reducible nor dihedral (F⁺ ⊆ F′ the real subfield of the splitting field of det ρ with μ_{p^∞}); there are σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F′) and σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F⁺) ∖ Gal(F_Σ/F′) whose ρ-eigenvalues have infinite order and lie in A; ρ ⊗ K̄ is irreducible on every finite-index normal subgroup of Gal(F_Σ/F⁺); and there is N_2 with λ^{n−(a−N_2)}𝒯_n ⊆ M for every submodule M ⊆ 𝒯_n = ad⁰ρ/λⁿ containing an m with λ^a m ≠ 0, a > N_2.
hypotheses: (6.2)(i)–(vi); characteristic of K is p.
proofSteps: Self-duality of W and the infinite-order element σ ∈ D_v force any decomposition of W to come from a quadratic character, making ρ induced; ρ|_{D_v} not split contradicts that (Lemma 6.1).
Lemma 6.3: finite-order eigenvalues in characteristic p on a pro-p image are 1; a unipotent τ and trace comparisons force triangularity otherwise; Hensel gives eigenvalues in A.
Lemma 6.5: A[G]x ⊇ λ^r ad⁰ρ with r = r(x) continuous, hence bounded.
acceptance: All representations here are over a characteristic-p DVR: finite-order means p-power, and 'dihedral' is tested over K̄.

sources.locator: §6, (6.1)–(6.2), p. 88 (Numdam PDF page 85; printed page = PDF page + 3)

nodes.title: Auxiliary prime sets in characteristic p
nodes.statement: (Proposition 6.10, with (6.3)–(6.11) and Lemmas 6.7–6.9.) With ρ as in char-p-adjoint-irreducibility and σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F′) whose ρ-eigenvalues lie in A and have infinite order, there is r = r(ρ) such that for every m > 0 there are infinitely many sets Q = {w_1, …, w_r} with Nm(w_i) ≡ 1 mod p^m, ρ(Frob_{w_i}) ≡ ρ(σ) mod λ^m, and lim_n H_{Σ_Q}(𝒯_n) ≅ (K/A)^r ⊕ X_{Σ_Q} with #X_{Σ_Q} < C(σ, r) independent of Q (Σ_Q = Σ_0 ∪ Q).
hypotheses: (6.2); the Selmer groups H_Σ(𝒯_n) use L_w = ker(H¹(D_w, 𝒯_n) → H_w(𝒯_n)) with H_v the ordinary condition at v | p and H_w the type-A/B condition at ramified w ∤ p.
proofSteps: Wiles' formula #H_Σ(𝒯_n)/#H*_Σ(𝒯_n) = h_∞∏h_w (6.3) ([W1, Proposition 1.6], generalised to totally real F; Poitou–Tate, ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4–R02.5); h_∞ ≍ #(A/λⁿ)^{2[F:ℚ]}, h_w ≍ 1 at type A/B places, h_v ≍ #(A/λⁿ)^{−2[F_v:ℚ_p]} (6.4)–(6.8), whence #H_Σ ≍ #H*_Σ·∏_{w∈Σ′}#H⁰(D_w, 𝒯_n(1)) (6.9).
(6.10)–(6.11) and Lemmas 6.7–6.8: the direct limits are (K/A)^r ⊕ finite.
Lemma 6.9 (after [W1, Proposition 1.11]): λ^{N_1} kills H¹(E_∞/F, 𝒯_n(1)) — a measure argument on the map σ ↦ lim σ^{1+p^n} with Lemma 6.4.
Choose primes w_j inductively by Chebotarev (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5) so that each kills a (K/A) summand of lim H*: after r steps lim H*_{Σ_r} is bounded, and (6.9) gives the claim.
acceptance: The coefficients are the characteristic-p DVR A: R04.5's finite-coefficient Taylor–Wiles primes are used only for the Chebotarev choice; the counting is done here.

nodes.title: The map ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) from deformation to Hecke rings
nodes.statement: (Lemma 7.1, Remark 7.2.) Let F have even degree, 𝒟 a deformation datum and 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟 (so 𝔭 comes from T^min_𝒟; A = the normalisation of T^min_𝒟/𝔭 ≅ k′[[λ]]). With Λ̃_𝒪 = 𝒪′[[W_1, …, W_m]] finite free over Λ_𝒪 (7.2), tilded rings R̃ = R ⊗_{Λ_𝒪} Λ̃_𝒪 and localisations-completions at primes 𝔭̃ over 𝔭, there is a natural local surjection ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} ↠ (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} with trace ρ^min(Frob_ℓ) ⊗ 1 ↦ T(ℓ) ⊗ 1 and det ρ^min(Frob_ℓ) ⊗ 1 ↦ S(ℓ)Nm(ℓ) ⊗ 1 for ℓ ∉ Σ; the same holds for the auxiliary data 𝒟_Q.
hypotheses: 𝔭 nice for 𝒟.
proofSteps: For each minimal Q ⊆ 𝔭̃ and each two-dimensional prime 𝔔 of the normalisation B of T̃/Q over a regular point of Λ̃_{𝒪,P}, Proposition 2.15 lifts the pseudo-deformation to (𝒪_j, Σ, c, ℳ)-minimal deformations ρ_j, giving maps from R̃^min.

Injectivity of the completed products (7.4)–(7.5) and Proposition 2.11 make R̃^ps → T̂_{𝔭_i} factor through R̃^min; the image in ∏(T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/Q is that of (T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}, giving the surjection (7.6).
acceptance: There is no natural map R^min → T^min: ψ exists only after localising and completing at a nice prime.

nodes.title: R = T at nice primes of minimal level
nodes.statement: (Proposition 7.3.) Let F be totally real of even degree, 𝒟 = 𝒟_c and 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 nice for 𝒟. Then (i) ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} → (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} is an isomorphism and (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} is a complete intersection over Λ̃_{𝒪,P} and reduced; (ii) M̃_{𝒟,𝔭̃} is a free (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃}-module.
hypotheses: F of even degree; 𝒟 = 𝒟_c (Σ = Σ_c, ℳ = ℳ_c = Σ_c ∖ 𝒫); 𝔭 nice.
proofSteps: Patching data: N^{(0)} = im(M̃_𝒟 → (M̃_𝒟)_{𝔭̃}/P) (7.7); R^{(0)}, R^{tr(0)} as images in (R̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/(𝔭̃F_0, P) (7.8)–(7.9) with F_0 the Fitting ideal; for odd N the sets Q_N of Proposition 6.10 give R^{(N)}_a, R^{tr(N)}_a (7.11)–(7.13) and M^{(N)}_a (7.10), with s_i = δ_{w_i} − 1 (Lemma 3.21).

Verification of (5.2)–(5.11): generator bounds from dim H¹(F_{Σ∪Q}/F, ad⁰ρ_c) and Lemma 2.10; freeness (5.10vi) via Lemma 3.19 after auxiliary Γ₁(ℓ_1⋯ℓ_s)-level at primes chosen by (7.15)–(7.16) with Lemma 3.29 and Corollary 3.6; the element x^{(N)} of (5.11) built in (7.21)–(7.25).

Proposition 5.9 gives R^{(0)} ⊗ K a complete intersection and Proposition 5.8 makes M^{(0)} ⊗ K free; with Lemma 5.2 (R^{tr(0)} ⊗ K ≅ R^{(0)} ⊗ K) and the surjection to (T̃^min)_{𝔭̃}/P, ψ mod P is an isomorphism; freeness of M̃ over Λ̃_{𝒪,P} lifts this to ψ and gives F_0 = 0 ((7.27)–(7.28)).
acceptance: Complete intersection and freeness are proved at the localisation-completion at 𝔭̃, not globally.

nodes.title: Congruence maps between levels
nodes.statement: (§8.2, Lemma 8.2 and (8.1).) For deformation data 𝒟_c = 𝒟_0 ≤ 𝒟_1 ≤ ⋯ ≤ 𝒟_n = 𝒟 (strict steps adding one place w_i, either to Σ or removing it from ℳ) and 𝔭 nice: R_i = (R̃^min_{𝒟_i})_{𝔭̃}, T_i, M_i and M⁺_i are free over Λ̃_{𝒪,P} with M_i^{2^s} ≅ Hom(M⁺_i, Λ̃_{𝒪,P})^{2^s} (Lemma 8.2); and there are T_i-maps Φ_i : M_{i−1}^{2^s r_i} → M_i^{2^s}, Φ̂_i, Ψ_i, Θ_i (r_i = 2 or 3) with Φ_i injective with Λ̃-free cokernel, Φ̂_i surjective, Θ_i∘Φ̂_i∘Φ_i∘Ψ_i = (unit·η_i *; 0 A_i) with det A_i not a zero divisor in T_0, and η_i = (q_i − 1)(T(ℓ_i)² − S(ℓ_i)(q_i + 1)²), (q_i − 1)(q_i + 1) or (q_i − 1) according as w_i ∈ Σ_i ∖ Σ_{i−1}, w_i ∈ ℳ_{i−1} with χ|_{I_{w_i}} = 1, or with χ|_{I_{w_i}} ≠ 1 (q_i = Nm(ℓ_i)).
hypotheses: 𝔭 nice for 𝒟.
proofSteps: Lemma 8.2 from Lemma 3.29 at auxiliary primes r_1, …, r_s and Proposition 3.3 with (3.17).
Φ_i = 2^s copies of f ↦ f + α_i g (+ α_i² h), with kernels and cokernels killed by T(ℓ) − 1 − Nm(ℓ) (Lemmas 3.26–3.28), hence trivial after localising at the non-Eisenstein 𝔭 (8.1a).
Explicit Ψ_i, Θ_i and the 3×3 matrix give the determinant (q_iS(ℓ_i)^{−2})^{2^s}η_i^{2^s−1} (8.1b).
acceptance: η_i is the level-raising congruence factor at w_i.

nodes.title: R = T at nice primes (all levels)
nodes.statement: (Proposition 8.1.) If 𝔭 ⊆ T_𝒟 is nice for 𝒟 (F of even degree), then ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} → (T̃^min_𝒟)_{𝔭̃} is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: F of even degree; 𝔭 nice for 𝒟.
proofSteps: For 𝒟 = 𝒟_c this is Proposition 7.3 (printed 'Proposition 7.2' on p. 119: E8). In general, compose the chain 𝒟_c ≤ ⋯ ≤ 𝒟 of §8.2; Lemma 8.4 cuts by a regular sequence y_1, …, y_{m−1} to a DVR C (8.3).
T′_0 is a reduced complete intersection over C, so ℓ_C(H_0/H_0²) = ℓ_C(C/δ(G_0)) (8.4) by de Smit–Rubin–Schoof Criterion I (R03.3).

The congruence maps give ℓ_C(C/(δ∘α)(G_n)) ≥ ℓ_C(C/δ(G_0)) + ℓ_C(C/δ(η)) (8.5); deformation theory gives ℓ_C(H_n/H_n²) ≤ ℓ_C(H_0/H_0²) + ℓ_C(C/δ(η)) (8.7), via Hom_C(R′_n, C ⊕ εC/λ^m) ↪ H¹(F_Σ/F, ad ρ/λ^m) (8.8) and the local count (8.10).
Hence ℓ_C(H_n/H_n²) ≤ ℓ_C(C/(δ∘α)(G_n)); DRS Criterion I makes R′_n → T″_n an isomorphism of complete intersections, and faithful flatness over B gives ψ(𝒟, 𝔭).
acceptance: This is the 'R = T' of the paper: it holds only after localisation and completion at a nice prime, and it uses the numerical (Wiles–Lenstra–de Smit–Rubin–Schoof) criterion, not an explicit presentation.

nodes.title: The crystalline representations V_{k,a_p}
nodes.statement: For k ≥ 2, a finite E/ℚ_p and a_p ∈ 𝔪_E, let D_{k,a_p} = Ee₁ ⊕ Ee₂ be the filtered φ-module with φ(e₁) = p^{k−1}e₂, φ(e₂) = −e₁ + a_pe₂, Fil^iD = D for i ≤ 0, Fil^iD = Ee₁ for 1 ≤ i ≤ k − 1 and Fil^iD = 0 for i ≥ k. It is weakly admissible, and V_{k,a_p} denotes the crystalline E-linear representation with D_cris(V*_{k,a_p}) = D_{k,a_p} (Colmez–Fontaine; BLZ construct it directly for a_p near 0). V_{k,a_p} is irreducible with Hodge–Tate weights 0 and k − 1, and the characteristic polynomial of φ is X² − a_pX + p^{k−1}. Every irreducible two-dimensional crystalline representation of G_{ℚ_p} is V_{k,a_p} ⊗ η for some k ≥ 2, a_p ∈ 𝔪_{ℚ̄_p} and crystalline character η (Breuil, Proposition 3.1.1 of JIMJ 2003, as recalled by BLZ).
hypotheses: a_p ∈ 𝔪_E, i.e. v_p(a_p) > 0: a unit a_p would give a unit-root φ-line, which is a weakly admissible subobject, so the representation would be reducible (ordinary)
BLZ work with V* (Hodge–Tate weights 0 and −(k − 1) in their convention); V has weights 0 and k − 1 with HT(χ) = +1
Breuil's classification is quoted by BLZ and was not read in its source (JIMJ 2 (2003))
proofSteps: A φ-stable line L (over a finite extension) has slope s ∈ (0, k − 1), because the roots of X² − a_pX + p^{k−1} have positive valuations when v_p(a_p) > 0; and L ≠ Fil¹ = Ee₁, because φ(e₁) = p^{k−1}e₂. So t_H(L) = 0 < s = t_N(L): D_{k,a_p} is weakly admissible and has no weakly admissible line, i.e. V_{k,a_p} is irreducible.
Colmez–Fontaine gives V_{k,a_p}; its Hodge–Tate weights are the filtration jumps 0 and k − 1.
acceptance: Check det V_{k,a_p}: det φ = p^{k−1}, so det V_{k,a_p} is χ^{k−1} times an unramified character
Check that a_p = 0, k = 2 is the Tate module of a supersingular elliptic curve with a_p = 0, e.g. y² = x³ − x at p = 3

nodes.title: Berger–Li–Zhu: reductions of V_{k,a_p} for small a_p
nodes.statement: Let k ≥ 2 and m = ⌊(k − 2)/(p − 1)⌋, except that for k = p + 1 one may take m = 0. There are P(X) ∈ M₂(ℤ_p[[π, X]]) and, for γ ∈ Γ_{ℚ_p}, G_γ(X) ∈ Id + πM₂(ℤ_p[[π, X]]) with P(X)φ(G_γ(X)) = G_γ(X)γ(P(X)) and G_{γη} = G_γγ(G_η), such that for every α ∈ 𝔪_E the pair (P(α), G_γ(α)) defines a Wach module N_{k,α} over 𝒪_E[[π]] with N_{k,α}/πN_{k,α}[1/p] ≅ D_{k,p^mα}. Consequently (Theorem 4.1) the reductions of the lattices T_{k,a_p} and T_{k,0} are isomorphic for a_p = p^mα, and (Corollary 4.3(1)) for k ≤ p + 1 and v_p(a_p) > 0, V̄_{k,a_p} ≅ V̄_{k,0} (semisimplified reductions). For k ≤ p this last statement is also a consequence of Fontaine–Laffaille.
hypotheses: m = 0 is allowed at k = p + 1 by Remark 4.2(1); this is what gives the endpoint weight p + 1

nodes.title: Crystalline with reducible reduction is ordinary (weights 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1)
nodes.statement: Let p be a prime, 2 ≤ k ≤ p + 1 and V : G_{ℚ_p} → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights {0, k − 1} whose semisimplified reduction V̄^{ss} is reducible. Then V is ordinary: V ≅ (ψ′χ^{k−1} ∗; 0 ψ) with ψ, ψ′ unramified, i.e. of Skinner–Wiles' shape with ψ₂ = ψ trivial on inertia. If moreover (p − 1) ∤ (k − 1) — for instance k = 2 with p ≥ 3, or k = p + 1 with p ≥ 3 — the two residual characters differ on D_p (p-distinguished). Proof: if V were not ordinary it would be irreducible (PadicHodgeTheory R06.4: for crystalline V, ordinary ⇔ reducible ⇔ unit root), hence V_{k,a_p} ⊗ η with v_p(a_p) > 0; then V̄^{ss} ≅ V̄_{k,0} ⊗ η̄ (BLZ Corollary 4.3(1)), which is irreducible (R21.5/reduction-of-v-k-zero) — a contradiction.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles over ℚ
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime and ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(ℚ̄_p) continuous, irreducible and unramified outside finitely many primes, with ρ̄^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ χ after a twist. If (i) χ|_{D_p} ≠ 1, (ii) ρ|_{I_p} ≅ (∗ ∗; 0 1), and (iii) det ρ = ψε^{k−1} for some k ≥ 2 and ψ of finite order, with det ρ odd, then ρ ≅ ρ_{f,λ} for a newform f of weight k. This is the theorem of Skinner–Wiles' introduction, and Theorem A with F = ℚ: ℚ is abelian, the splitting field of the character χ is abelian over ℚ, χ is odd because det ρ is, and (ii) gives the nearly ordinary shape with ψ₂^{(p)} trivial on I_p (its reduction is 1, so it factors through a pro-p group).

nodes.title: The ordinary theorems do not use Serre's conjecture
nodes.statement: The prerequisite closure of R21.5/theorem-a (and so of its specialisations and of R21.6's export) contains no node of ClassicalSerreModularity and no modularity assertion about a residually irreducible representation. Its inputs are: the nearly ordinary Hecke algebras (R21.1–R21.2, PadicFamilies); Wiles' Galois representations and Carayol's local-global compatibility (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19); pseudo-representations and deformation rings (R21.3); patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3–R03.6, GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5); the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3); solvable base change (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4); and Washington, Waldschmidt and Raynaud (gaps). The residual representation is reducible, and its "modularity" is by an Eisenstein series, through the permissible maximal ideal (R21.2), not by Serre's conjecture. So the theorems may initialise Serre's conjecture (Khare's level one, the modern p = 3 branch) without circularity.

nodes.title: Deformation data for an absolutely irreducible nearly ordinary ρ₀
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real of degree d, p odd, v_1, …, v_t the places above p with decomposition groups D_i, and k finite of characteristic p. A residual representation ρ₀ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(k) satisfies (2.1) if (i) ρ₀ is absolutely irreducible; (ii) det ρ₀(z_i) = −1 for every complex conjugation z_i; (iii) ρ₀|_{D_i} ≅ (χ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 χ^{(i)}_2) with χ^{(i)}_1 ≠ χ^{(i)}_2 for every i (the extension may be nonsplit; when it splits a labelling is fixed); (iv) if ρ₀ is ramified at v ∤ p∞ then ρ₀|_{D_v} ≅ (1 *; 0 ω^{−1}). A deformation datum is 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, ℳ): 𝒪 the integers of a local field with residue field k, Σ a finite set of finite places containing 𝒫 = {v_1, …, v_t} and the places where ρ₀ ramifies, and ℳ ⊆ Σ ∖ 𝒫 a set of places where ρ₀ ramifies; Σ₀ = 𝒫 ∪ {ramified places}, ℳ₀ = Σ₀ ∖ 𝒫 and 𝒟₀ = (𝒪, Σ₀, ℳ₀) is the minimal datum. A deformation ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(A) is of type 𝒟 if A is an 𝒪-algebra, ρ is unramified outside Σ and ∞, ρ|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_1 ≡ χ^{(i)}_1 mod m_A, and ρ|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) for w ∈ ℳ. The universal deformation of type 𝒟 is ρ_𝒟 : Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(R_𝒟). For Q disjoint from Σ, type 𝒟_Q allows ramification at Q with det ρ unramified there, giving R_{𝒟_Q}; 𝒟_Q-minimality (det ρ trivial on the torsion N_Σ of Gal(L_Σ/F)) gives R^min_{𝒟_Q}, and (2.2) R_{𝒟_Q} ≅ R^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[N_Σ], ρ_{𝒟_Q} ≅ ρ^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗ Ψ_Σ. For Σ ⊆ Σ′ and ℳ′ ⊆ ℳ the natural map R_{𝒟′} ↠ R_𝒟 is a map of Λ_𝒪-algebras (the Λ_𝒪-structure of R21.3/deformation-iwasawa-algebra, with T_i ↦ det ρ_𝒟(γ_i) − 1 and Y^{(i)}_j ↦ ψ^{(i)}_2(y^{(i)}_j) − 1).
hypotheses: p odd; ω is the mod-p cyclotomic character, unramified at v ∤ p, so (iv) gives ρ₀|_{I_v} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) and the ℳ-condition lifts it
unlike R21.3/deformation-datum there is no extension class c and no residual χ ⊕ 1: ρ₀ is fixed and absolutely irreducible, and ρ₀|_{D_i} may be nonsplit
proofSteps: Absolute irreducibility makes the deformation functor pro-representable (Mazur; GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2).

The type-𝒟 conditions are deformation conditions: the nearly ordinary condition at v_i is the ordered-flag condition with the χ^{(i)}_1-line as sub (LocalGaloisDeformationRings L8), and ρ|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) is stable under fibre products.
Type 𝒟_Q and minimality exactly as in Skinner–Wiles 1999 §2.3 (R21.3/deformation-of-type): N_Σ is a finite p-group and p is odd, so ρ^min ⊗ Ψ_Σ is universal for type 𝒟_Q.

nodes.title: Dihedral deformations and the dimension of the dihedral locus (Lemma 2.2)
nodes.statement: A deformation ρ of ρ₀ is dihedral if ρ|_{Gal(F̄/F′)} factors through an abelian quotient for some quadratic F′/F; equivalently for some abelian L/F (2.3)(i), and only if ρ₀ is dihedral (2.3)(ii), which determines F′. If ρ₀ = Ind_{F′}^F ψ₀ (2.4), with ψ₀ distinct from its conjugate ψ₀′, every dihedral deformation is Ind_{F′}^F Ψ with Ψ ≡ ψ₀. With Γ_Σ = Gal(L′_Σ/F′) (L′_Σ the maximal abelian pro-p extension of F′ unramified outside Σ), ψ the projection onto Γ_Σ and Ψ_Σ = ψ̃₀ψ : Gal(F_Σ/F′) → 𝒪[[Γ_Σ]]^×, Ind_{F′}^F Ψ_Σ is the universal dihedral deformation of type (𝒪, Σ, ℳ) when every place above p splits in F′ and ℳ = ∅, and surjects onto it otherwise. Let δ⁻_{F′} be the ℤ_p-rank of the summand of Γ_Σ on which Gal(F′/F) acts by −1. (Lemma 2.2, first inequality.) If q ⊆ R_𝒟 is a prime containing p with ρ_𝒟 mod q dihedral of finite-order determinant, then dim R_𝒟/q ≤ δ⁻_{F′}. (Second inequality.) If F′ is totally real, δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2. If F′ is CM, δ⁻_{F′} = d, and the bound dim R_𝒟/q ≤ d/2 printed in Lemma 2.2 fails when every place above p splits in F′ and ℳ = ∅ (source issue OrdinaryAutomorphicFormsAndModularityLifting/E11).
hypotheses: Skinner–Wiles print 'By [Wal] we know that δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2' for every F′; [Wal] is absent from their bibliography and is Skinner–Wiles 1999's [Wal] (Waldschmidt), a gap of this roadmap
for F′ totally real the minus part of the units of F′ has ℤ-rank d, and Waldschmidt's bound (p-adic rank at least half the rank) gives δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2
for F′ CM the minus part of the units is finite, while the minus part of the local units at the places above p has ℤ_p-rank d, so δ⁻_{F′} = d
proofSteps: A dihedral ρ over a domain A of characteristic p with det ρ of finite order is Ind Ψ with ΨΨ′ of finite order, so Ψ = ψ̃₀·ψ⁻ with ψ⁻ factoring (up to a finite group) through the minus part of Γ_Σ.
R_𝒟/q is topologically generated by traces (R21.3/irreducible-trace-generation), which lie in the image of k′[[Γ_Σ⁻]]; hence dim R_𝒟/q ≤ δ⁻_{F′}.
Class field theory: rank Γ_Σ = [F′ : ℚ] − (p-adic rank of the units of F′) (up to the Leopoldt defect of F on the plus side); split into ± parts under Gal(F′/F).

Counterexample to the printed d/2 for CM F′, all v | p split, ℳ = ∅: Ind(ψ̃₀ψ⁻) over k[[Γ_Σ⁻]] is of type 𝒟 (nearly ordinary at each split v_i as Ψ|_{D_w} ⊕ Ψ|_{D_w̄}), has finite-order determinant, and its trace ring has dimension d.
acceptance: The totally real case is the one Skinner–Wiles' citation covers; do not use the d/2 bound for CM F′.
Check the CM rank count on a small case: F = ℚ, F′ imaginary quadratic, δ⁻ = 1 > 1/2.

nodes.title: R_{𝒟_Q} is generated over Λ_𝒪 by traces of Frobenius (Lemma 2.3)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 2.3.) If 𝒟_Q = (𝒪, Σ, ℳ)_Q is any augmented deformation datum and S is any finite set of places containing Σ ∪ Q, then R_{𝒟_Q} is generated as a Λ_𝒪-algebra by {trace ρ_{𝒟_Q}(Frob_ℓ) : ℓ ∉ S}.
hypotheses: ρ₀ absolutely irreducible (2.1)(i)
proofSteps: Carayol: for absolutely irreducible ρ₀ the universal deformation is defined over the closed subring generated by its traces (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem), so the universal property forces R_{𝒟_Q} to be that subring.
Chebotarev: the Frobenius elements at ℓ ∉ S are dense, so their traces generate the trace ring topologically; the Λ_𝒪-structure only adds the variables T_i and Y^{(i)}_j.
acceptance: This is the irreducible-residual replacement for the pseudo-representation arguments of R21.3/matrix-entry-subring; no pseudo-deformation ring is needed.

nodes.title: The Galois representation over T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m for irreducible ρ_m
nodes.statement: Assume (H_even): [F : ℚ] is even. For a maximal ideal m of T_∞(U, 𝒪) (R21.1/quaternionic-nearly-ordinary-hecke-algebra) there is ρ_{U,m} : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m ⊗_{Λ′_𝒪} F_{Λ′_𝒪}) satisfying the properties (3.2) of R21.3/hida-family-representation without 'mod Q'. If the residual representation ρ_m is irreducible, then in a suitable basis ρ_{U,m} takes values in GL₂(T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m), and T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is a Λ_𝒪-algebra through 1 + T_i ↦ det ρ_{U,m}(γ_i) and 1 + Y^{(i)}_j ↦ T_{y^{(i)}_j}, with Λ_𝒪 finite and free over Λ′_𝒪. (Lemma 3.3.) (i) For any finite S ⊇ Σ(U) (the places w with U_w ≠ GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}), together with 𝒫), T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m is generated over Λ_𝒪 by {T(ℓ) : ℓ ∉ S}; (ii) if U is sufficiently small, M_∞(U)_m and M⁺_∞(U)_m are free Λ_𝒪-modules of equal rank.
hypotheses: (H_even) is needed for the definite quaternionic modules of R21.1
U sufficiently small means U ⊆ U₁(ℓ_1 ⋯ ℓ_s) for unramified primes as in Skinner–Wiles 1999 Corollary 3.6
proofSteps: Glue the ρ_Q of R21.3/hida-family-representation over the minimal primes Q of T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m to a representation over the total ring of fractions.
If ρ_m is irreducible, the traces lie in T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m and Carayol's theorem (Wiles 1995, pp. 482–483; GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem) gives an integral model.
Lemma 3.3(i) as Skinner–Wiles 1999 Lemma 3.11 (R21.3/hecke-generation), with traces in place of the pseudo-representation; (ii) from (i) and PadicFamilies L5/hida-freeness.
acceptance: Integrality is claimed only when ρ_m is irreducible; for residually reducible m use R21.3/hecke-pseudo-representation.

nodes.title: Permissible levels U_{𝒟_Q}, (H_def) and the Hecke rings T_{𝒟_Q}
nodes.statement: A maximal ideal m of T_∞(U, 𝒪) is permissible if ρ_m ≅ ρ₀ and T_0(𝔭_i) − χ^{(i)}_2(λ_{𝔭_i}) ∈ m for 1 ≤ i ≤ t (it is then unique; the uniformisers λ_{𝔭_i} are chosen with (χ^{(i)}_1/χ^{(i)}_2)(λ_{𝔭_i}) ≠ 1). For an augmented datum 𝒟_Q = (𝒪, Σ, ℳ)_Q let U_{𝒟_Q} = ∏_{w∤∞} U_{𝒟_Q,w} with U_{𝒟_Q,w} = GL₂(𝒪_{F,w}) for w ∉ Σ ∖ 𝒫 ∪ Q; {(a b; c d) : c, a − 1 ∈ ℓ_w²} for w ∈ Σ ∖ (𝒫 ∪ ℳ); {c ∈ ℓ_w, a mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ_w} for w ∈ ℳ; and {c ∈ ℓ_w, ad^{−1} mod ℓ_w ∈ Δ′_w} for w ∈ Q, where Δ_w is the Sylow p-subgroup of (𝒪_F/ℓ_w)^× and Δ′_w a complement. (H_def): T_∞(U_{𝒟₀}, 𝒪) has a permissible maximal ideal; then so does every T_∞(U_{𝒟_Q}, 𝒪). Put T_{𝒟_Q} = T_∞(U_{𝒟_Q}, 𝒪)_m, T_𝒟 = T_{𝒟_∅}, and ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} the representation of R21.3/integral-hecke-galois-representation in a basis with ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} mod m = ρ₀. The T_{𝒟_Q}-modules M_{𝒟_Q}, M⁺_{𝒟_Q} are those of Skinner–Wiles 1999 after Lemma 3.25 with ℳ_c replaced by ℳ₀ and r(w) = 1 (localisations of M_∞(U^min_{𝒟_Q}), M⁺_∞(U^min_{𝒟_Q}) at m), with the commuting action of Δ_Q = ∏_{w∈Q} Δ_w, generators δ_w and σ_w ∈ I_w mapping to δ_w; T^min_{𝒟_Q} is the quotient of Skinner–Wiles 1999 §3.6 (essentially the largest reduced quotient through which R_{𝒟_Q} → T_{𝒟_Q} factors via R^min_{𝒟_Q}), with the 𝒟_Q-minimal ρ^mod_{𝒟^min_Q}.
hypotheses: (H_even) and (H_def)
proofSteps: U_{𝒟_Q} ⊆ U_{𝒟₀}, so a permissible maximal ideal at level U_{𝒟₀} pulls back to every U_{𝒟_Q}.
Uniqueness of m: ρ_m ≅ ρ₀ fixes the T(ℓ) mod m, and T_0(𝔭_i) mod m is fixed as χ^{(i)}_2(λ_{𝔭_i}) (the other root χ^{(i)}_1(λ_{𝔭_i}) is distinct by the choice of λ_{𝔭_i}).
The modules and T^min are Skinner–Wiles 1999's (R21.2/deformation-hecke-rings) with the stated substitutions.
acceptance: (H_def) is an assumption here; Theorem 5.1 obtains it after base change from Skinner–Wiles, Base change and a problem of Serre (a gap).

nodes.title: ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} is of type 𝒟_Q and R_{𝒟_Q} ↠ T_{𝒟_Q} (Proposition 3.4)
nodes.statement: (Proposition 3.4.) Under (H_even) and (H_def), ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} is a deformation of ρ₀ of type 𝒟_Q, and the corresponding map r_{𝒟_Q} : R_{𝒟_Q} → T_{𝒟_Q} is a surjection of Λ_𝒪-algebras.
hypotheses: (H_even) and (H_def); ρ₀ absolutely irreducible
proofSteps: For each minimal prime P of T_{𝒟_Q} put ρ_P = ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} mod P. det ρ_P is unramified at w ∈ Q: reduce modulo algebraic primes and use local–global compatibility (Proposition 3.2 = PadicFamilies L5/hida-control-nearly-ordinary; AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4).

At v_i: choose σ_i ∈ D_i mapping to λ_{𝔭_i}; in a basis with ρ_P(σ_i) = diag(α, β), α ≡ χ^{(i)}_1(λ_{𝔭_i}), (3.2)(vi) and T_0(𝔭_i) − χ^{(i)}_2(λ_{𝔭_i}) ∈ m give ρ_P|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_2 ≡ χ^{(i)}_2.

At w ∈ ℳ: at algebraic points ρ_π|_{D_w} is unramified or of Type A (R21.3/ramification-types) by the level U_{𝒟_Q,w}; the argument of Skinner–Wiles 1999 Proposition 3.13 (R21.3/level-type-control) transfers this to ρ_P ⊗ L; ρ₀ ramified at w excludes unramified, so (ρ_P ⊗ L)|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) with * ≠ 0. For σ ∈ I_w a generator of pro-p tame inertia, (σ − 1)² kills a free rank-two R-lattice M, N = M/M[σ − 1] reduces to a one-dimensional quotient of ρ₀, so N ≅ R and M[σ − 1] ≅ R, giving ρ_P|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1) integrally.

The maps r_P : R_{𝒟_Q} → T_{𝒟_Q}/P assemble to r_{𝒟_Q} : R_{𝒟_Q} → ∏_P T_{𝒟_Q}/P (3.3); its image is T_{𝒟_Q} because traces of Frobenius map to the T(ℓ) (R21.3/irreducible-trace-generation and Lemma 3.3(i)).
The induced representation into GL₂(T_{𝒟_Q}) agrees with ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} modulo every minimal prime, so they are equal (T_{𝒟_Q} reduced); hence ρ^mod_{𝒟_Q} is of type 𝒟_Q.
acceptance: The surjection is onto the full Hecke ring, not only onto a trace subring; compare R21.3/hecke-generation, which in the reducible case goes through pseudo-deformations.

nodes.title: T_{𝒟_Q} ≅ T^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗ 𝒪[N_Σ] and the trace at auxiliary primes (Lemma 3.5)
nodes.statement: (Lemma 3.5.) (i) There is an isomorphism T_{𝒟_Q} ≅ T^min_{𝒟_Q} ⊗_𝒪 𝒪[N_Σ] compatible with r_{𝒟_Q}, r^min_{𝒟_Q} and (2.2). (ii) T^min_{𝒟_Q} is a finite, reduced, torsion-free Λ_𝒪-algebra. (iii) For each w ∈ Q, trace ρ^mod_{𝒟^min_Q}(σ_w) acts on M_{𝒟_Q} and M⁺_{𝒟_Q} as δ_w + δ_w^{−1}. The map r^min_{𝒟_Q} : R^min_{𝒟_Q} → T^min_{𝒟_Q} is surjective by Proposition 3.4.
hypotheses: (H_even) and (H_def)
proofSteps: From the definition of T^min_{𝒟_Q} and the arguments of Skinner–Wiles 1999 Proposition 3.23 and Lemmas 3.21 and 3.25 (R21.2/minimal-hecke-ring-decomposition, R21.2/auxiliary-trace-identity).
Surjectivity of r^min from R21.3/irreducible-hecke-surjection and (2.2).
acceptance: (iii) is the identity the patching argument uses to make M_{𝒟_Q} a module over 𝒪[[s_1, …, s_r]] through s_i = δ_{w_i} − 1 compatibly with t_i = trace(ρ(σ_{w_i})) − 2.

nodes.title: Good pairs, nice primes and property (P) for irreducible ρ₀
nodes.statement: (F, ρ₀) is a good pair if (i) d/2 > 2 + 2t + 7·#ℳ₀, (ii) d_i > 2 + 2t + 7·#ℳ₀ for i = 1, …, t (d_i = [F_{v_i} : ℚ_p]), and (iii) (H_even) and (H_def) hold (4.1). A prime q of R_𝒟 is pro-modular if it is the inverse image under r_𝒟 of a prime of T_𝒟 (R21.4/pro-modular-prime); a deformation over a domain is pro-modular if its kernel is. A prime 𝔭 of R_𝒟 is nice for 𝒟 if (4.2): (i) 𝔭 is a dimension-one prime containing p; (ii) ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭 is not dihedral and det ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭 has finite order; (iii) for each v_i, (ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭)|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_1/ψ^{(i)}_2 of infinite order; (iv) 𝔭 is the inverse image of a prime of T_{𝒟₀}. A prime with (i)–(iii) and ρ_𝒟 mod 𝔭 of type 𝒟₀ is merely nice. Property (P) for 𝒟: if 𝔭 is nice for 𝒟, every prime q ⊆ 𝔭 is pro-modular.
hypotheses: the good-pair inequalities depend only on (F, ρ₀), not on Σ; see source issue E14 for the bound on #Σ that Proposition 4.1's proof also needs
proofSteps: Pro-modularity of q is equivalent to a map θ_q : T_𝒟 → R_𝒟/q with θ_q ∘ r_𝒟 the reduction modulo q.
acceptance: Compare with R21.4/good-pair-and-nice-primes: one property (P) replaces (P1) and (P2), and there is no p-adic L-function or class-group condition.

nodes.title: Every prime of R_𝒟 is pro-modular (Proposition 4.1, irreducible ρ₀)
nodes.statement: (Proposition 4.1.) Let (F, ρ₀) be a good pair and 𝒟 = (𝒪, Σ, ℳ) a deformation datum, and assume (a) d/2 > 2 + 2t + 7·#(Σ ∖ 𝒫) (source issue E14; for Σ = Σ₀ this is (4.1)(i)) and (b) if ρ₀ ≅ Ind_{F′}^F ψ₀ is dihedral, the dihedral deformations of type 𝒟′ with finite-order determinant have dimension at most d/2 for every 𝒟′ below (true when F′ is totally real; source issue E11). If (P) holds for every datum (𝒪, Σ′, ℳ′) with ℳ ⊆ ℳ′ and Σ′ ⊆ Σ, then every prime of R_𝒟 is pro-modular.
hypotheses: Skinner–Wiles state the proposition without (a) and (b); their proof uses both (source issues E11 and E14)
in the application (R21.5/nearly-ordinary-irreducible-lifting) (a) holds because L is chosen with d_L/2 > 2 + 7·#Σ_L
proofSteps: 𝒟 = 𝒟₀, step one: T_{𝒟₀} is finite torsion-free over Λ_𝒪 (Lemma 3.1), so for a minimal prime Q of R = T_{𝒟₀}/(p, T_1, …, T_{δ_F}), R/Q is integral over k[[Y^{(i)}_j]] and has dimension d; by (b) ρ^mod mod Q is not dihedral, and infinitely many dimension-one primes avoiding the Y^{(i)}_1 give a prime nice for 𝒟₀ ((3.2)(vi)).
Step two: by (P) every component of Spec R_{𝒟₀} through a nice prime is pro-modular, so C^mod_{𝒟₀} ≠ ∅.

Step three: if C′ = C_{𝒟₀} ∖ C^mod_{𝒟₀} ≠ ∅, Proposition 2.1 and Corollary A.2 (R21.4/raynaud-connectedness-corollary) give C_1 ∈ C^mod, C_2 ∈ C′ meeting in Q of dimension d − 2t + δ_F − 3#ℳ₀; a minimal Q_1 over (Q, p, det ρ(γ_i) − 1) has dimension ≥ d − 2t − 3#ℳ₀ − 1 > 1 + d/2 by (4.1), so ρ mod Q_1 is not dihedral by (b); Q_1 is pro-modular; if Q^mod_1 contained all Y^{(i)}_j then d_i ≤ 2t + 3#ℳ₀ + 1, contradicting (4.1)(ii); a dimension-one 𝔭 ⊇ Q_1 avoiding the Y^{(i)}_1 is nice, so C_2 is pro-modular by step two: contradiction.

General 𝒟: a nice prime of R_𝒟 comes from a nice prime of R_{𝒟₀}, and composing θ with T_𝒟 ↠ T_{𝒟₀} shows it is nice for 𝒟, so (P) makes its components pro-modular. For a minimal prime Q of R_𝒟, choose τ_v and a basis at each v ∈ Σ ∖ 𝒫 and let I_2 = (p; a_v − 1, b_v − u_v, c_v, d_v − 1; det ρ_𝒟(γ_j) − 1); a minimal Q_2 over (Q, I_2) has dimension ≥ d − 2t − 3#ℳ − 4#(Σ ∖ 𝒫) ≥ d/2 + 1 by (a), so ρ mod Q_2 is not dihedral by (b), is of type 𝒟₀, and lies in a nice prime; hence Q is pro-modular.
acceptance: Check each inequality in the Lean file: step three's bound from (4.1)(i), the contradiction with (4.1)(ii), and that (4.1) alone does not give the bound of the general step (E14).
No R = T isomorphism is claimed here; that is property (P).

nodes.title: Selmer groups and auxiliary primes in characteristic p (Lemma 7.1, Proposition 7.2)
nodes.statement: Let ρ : G_Σ = Gal(F_Σ/F) → GL₂(A), A ≅ k[[λ]], with ρ ⊗ K̄ irreducible and not dihedral, ρ mod λ = ρ₀, Σ ⊇ 𝒫 ∪ {ramified places of ρ₀}, ρ ramified at w ∤ p exactly where ρ₀ is and then ρ|_{I_w} ≅ (1 *; 0 1), det ρ = det ρ₀, and ρ|_{D_v} ≅ (χ^{(v)}_1 *; 0 χ^{(v)}_2) with χ^{(v)}_1/χ^{(v)}_2 of infinite order for v | p. Let F′ be the splitting field of det ρ with all p-power roots of unity adjoined and F⁺ its fixed field under z_1. (Lemma 7.1.) There are σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F′), and σ ∈ Gal(F_Σ/F⁺) ∖ Gal(F_Σ/F′), such that the eigenvalues of ρ(σ) lie in A and have infinite order. With 𝒰 the space of ρ, the filtrations 𝒰_{1,i} at v_i and 𝒰^w_1 at ramified w ∤ p, 𝒯 = {f ∈ ad ρ : trace f = 0}, 𝒯^{ord}_{v_i}, 𝒯^w and 𝒯_n = 𝒯/λⁿ, put H_{v_i}(𝒯_n) = H¹(I_i, 𝒯_n/𝒯^{ord}_{n,i}), H_w(𝒯_n) = H¹(I_w, 𝒯_n/𝒯^w_n) (0 if ρ₀ is unramified at w), L_w = ker(H¹(D_w, 𝒯_n) → H_w(𝒯_n)) and H_Σ(𝒯_n) the classes locally in L_w for all w ∈ Σ. (Proposition 7.2.) For σ as in Lemma 7.1(i) there is r = r(ρ) such that for every m > 0 there are infinitely many Q = {w_1, …, w_r} with (i) Nm(w_i) ≡ 1 mod p^m, (ii) ρ_𝔭(Frob_{w_i}) ≡ ρ_𝔭(σ) mod λ^m, and (iii) lim_n H_{Σ_Q}(𝒯_n) ≅ (K/A)^r ⊕ X_{Σ_Q} with Σ_Q = Σ₀ ∪ Q and #X_{Σ_Q} < C(σ, r) depending only on σ and r.
hypotheses: A is a characteristic-p discrete valuation ring; K = Frac A
not dihedral replaces the proof of non-dihedrality needed in the reducible case
proofSteps: Lemma 7.1 exactly as Skinner–Wiles 1999 Lemma 6.3 (R21.4/char-p-adjoint-irreducibility); here ρ is assumed non-dihedral from the start.

Proposition 7.2 exactly as Skinner–Wiles 1999 Proposition 6.10 (R21.4/auxiliary-prime-sets): Wiles' Selmer formula (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.4, R02.5) and Chebotarev (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.5).
acceptance: The Selmer groups use the ordinary line 𝒰_{1,i} at v_i and the unipotent line at ramified w ∤ p, matching type 𝒟₀.

nodes.title: R = T at nice primes and property (P) (Propositions 8.1–8.2)
nodes.statement: Assume (H_even) and (H_def). (Proposition 8.1.) If 𝔭 ⊆ T_{𝒟₀} is nice for 𝒟₀, then (i) ψ(𝒟₀, 𝔭) : (R̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ → (T̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ is an isomorphism and (R̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ is a reduced complete intersection over Λ̃_{𝒪,P}; (ii) M̃_{𝒟₀,𝔭̃} is a free (T̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃-module. Here the integral closure of T^min_𝒟/𝔭 is A ≅ k′[[λ]], finite over Λ_𝒪 = 𝒪[[z_1, …, z_m]] with z_i ↦ λ^{r_i}u_i (r_i > 0, u_1 a unit), Λ̃_𝒪 = 𝒪′[[W_1, …, W_m]] → A by W_1 ↦ λ, W_i ↦ 0, Λ_𝒪 → Λ̃_𝒪 by z_1 ↦ W_1^{r_1}ũ_1, z_i ↦ −W_i + W_1^{r_i}ũ_i, tildes denote base change to Λ̃_𝒪, 𝔭̃ a prime above 𝔭, and P = (π, W_2, …, W_m). (Proposition 8.2.) For every datum 𝒟 and every prime 𝔭 ⊆ R_𝒟 nice for 𝒟, ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) is an isomorphism and property (P) holds for 𝔭.
hypotheses: the map ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) is Skinner–Wiles 1999's (R21.4/minimum-level-surjection) with the irreducible data
proofSteps: Rings and modules: N^{(0)} = im(M̃_𝒟 → (M̃_𝒟)_𝔭̃/P) and R^{(0)} = im(R̃^min_𝒟 → (R̃^min_𝒟)_𝔭̃/(𝔭̃F_0, P)) with F_0 the Fitting ideal of (M̃_𝒟)_𝔭̃; for odd N the sets Q_N of Proposition 7.2 (R21.4/irreducible-selmer-auxiliary-primes) give M^{(N)}_a over A_a = A[[s_1, …, s_r]]/(s_i^{a+1}), s_i = δ_{w_i} − 1, and R^{(N)}_a over B_a via t_i ↦ trace(ρ_{𝒟_Q}(σ_{w_i}) − 2) ⊗ 1, with R^{(N)}_0 = R^{(0)}, M^{(0)} = ⊕_{i=1}^{2^r} N^{(0)} and M^{(N)}_0 = M^{(0)} (8.1).

Verify (6.2)–(6.8): the number of generators is bounded by dim_k H¹(F_{Σ∪Q}/F, ad⁰ρ₀); (6.7)(vi) from Skinner–Wiles 1999 Lemma 3.19 (R21.2/auxiliary-level-freeness) after shrinking U^min_{𝒟_Q}; d(a) = d_1(a)d_1(1) + 1; (6.5ii) from Proposition 7.2(iii) and 𝔛_Q = Hom_A((𝔭̃^min_{𝒟_Q}/(𝔭̃^min_{𝒟_Q})², P), λ^{−n}A/A) ≅ H_{Σ_Q}(𝒯_n); x^{(N)} as in Skinner–Wiles 1999 §7; Lemma 3.5(iii) (R21.3/irreducible-minimal-hecke-quotient) for compatibility of the A_a- and B_a-structures.
Proposition 6.1 (Skinner–Wiles 1999 Propositions 5.8–5.9 with R^{tr} = R; R21.4/formal-patching-theorem): R^{(0)} ⊗_A K is a complete intersection and M^{(0)} ⊗_A K is free over it.

Hence (T̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃^s → (M̃_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ (8.2) is an isomorphism, (T̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ is free over Λ̃_{𝒪,P}, (8.3) is an isomorphism, F_0 = 0, and (R̃^min_{𝒟₀})_𝔭̃ is a complete intersection; T^min is reduced (Lemma 3.5(ii)).

Proposition 8.2: ψ(𝒟, 𝔭) is an isomorphism for every 𝒟 by the congruences of Skinner–Wiles 1999 §3.8 (R21.4/level-raising-congruence-maps), and property (P) follows as in their Proposition 8.4 (R21.4/property-p1).
acceptance: The rings are localised and completed at 𝔭̃ and the isomorphism is after base change to Λ̃_𝒪; a formalisation must keep both, as in R21.4/nice-prime-r-equals-t.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles lifting for irreducible residual representations over totally real fields (Theorem 5.1)
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, p odd, and ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL₂(Q̄_p) satisfy (5.1): continuous and irreducible, unramified outside a finite set Σ, det ρ(τ) = −1 for every complex conjugation τ, det ρ = ψε^μ with μ ≥ 1 and ψ of finite order, and ρ|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 ψ^{(i)}_2) with ψ^{(i)}_2|_{I_i} of finite order for each v_i | p. Call ρ D_i-distinguished if ρ̄^{ss}|_{D_i} ≅ (χ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 χ^{(i)}_2) with χ^{(i)}_1 ≠ χ^{(i)}_2, labelled so that χ^{(i)}_2 = ψ^{(i)}_2 mod λ; another ρ′ satisfying (5.1) is a χ₂-good lift of ρ̄^{ss} if (ρ̄′)^{ss} ≅ ρ̄^{ss} and ρ′|_{D_i} ≅ (φ^{(i)}_1 *; 0 φ^{(i)}_2) with φ^{(i)}_2 reducing to χ^{(i)}_2. (Theorem 5.1.) If (i) ρ̄^{ss} is irreducible and D_i-distinguished for all i, (ii) there is a nearly ordinary automorphic representation π₀ of GL₂/F with ρ_{π₀} a χ₂-good lift of ρ̄^{ss}, and (iii) ρ̄^{ss} is not induced from a quadratic extension F′/F with a complex place (the hypothesis the printed proof needs; source issue E11), then ρ ≅ ρ_π for an automorphic representation π.
hypotheses: Skinner–Wiles state the theorem without (iii); their proof, through Lemma 2.2, covers a dihedral ρ̄^{ss} only when the dihedral locus has dimension at most d_L/2, which holds for F′ totally real and fails for CM F′ in which the places above p split (E11)
ρ̄^{ss} is allowed to be reducible on Gal(F̄/F(ζ_p)): these are the cases Wiles, Diamond and Fujiwara exclude
the base change input, Skinner–Wiles, Base change and a problem of Serre (Duke Math. J. 107 (2001)), is a gap
proofSteps: Choose 𝒪, λ, k with ρ valued in GL₂(𝒪), and ρ̄^{ss} = Ind_{F′}^F ψ₀ if dihedral. By the main result of Skinner–Wiles, Base change and a problem of Serre, and hypothesis (ii), there is a totally real L/F with solvable Galois closure over F such that ρ₀ = ρ̄^{ss}|_{Gal(F̄/L)} satisfies (2.1) and (H_even), (H_def) hold for L and ρ₀.

Enlarge L by a large real subfield of a cyclotomic extension so that d_L/2 > 2 + 7·#Σ_L and d_v > 2 + 7·#Σ_L for v | p; then (L, ρ₀) is a good pair and Proposition 4.1's extra bound (E14) holds (checked in the Lean file).

ρ_1 = ρ|_{Gal(F̄/L)} is of type 𝒟_L = (𝒪, Σ_L, ∅); (P) holds by Proposition 8.2 (R21.4/irreducible-nice-prime-r-equals-t), so ρ_1 is pro-modular by Proposition 4.1 (R21.4/irreducible-pro-modularity), and the homomorphism T_{𝒟_L} → 𝒪 is algebraic.

Proposition 3.2 (PadicFamilies L5/hida-control-nearly-ordinary) gives ρ_1 ≅ ρ_{π_1} for a nearly ordinary π_1 of GL₂/L; solvable base change and descent (GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer R17.4) give π over F.
acceptance: Record the hypotheses individually: p odd, (5.1)(i)–(v), D_i-distinguishedness, the χ₂-good nearly ordinary π₀, and (iii).

This serves the requests of GL2ModularityLifting R22.1 (ordinary lifting over totally real F) and of PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R23.3 (Taylor's ordinary case), with D_i-distinguishedness as an explicit hypothesis.

nodes.title: Skinner–Wiles over ℚ for irreducible residual representations (Theorem 5.2 and the introduction)
nodes.statement: Let p be odd and ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(E) (E/ℚ_p finite) continuous, irreducible and unramified outside finitely many primes, with (i) ρ̄^{ss} irreducible, (ii) ρ̄^{ss}|_{D_p} ≅ (χ_1 *; 0 χ_2) with (χ_1/χ_2)|_{D_p} ≠ 1, (iii) ρ̄^{ss} modular, (iv) ρ|_{I_p} ≅ (* *; 0 1), (v) det ρ = ψε^{k−1} with k ≥ 2 and ψ of finite order, det ρ odd. If moreover ρ̄^{ss} is not induced from an imaginary quadratic field (the hypothesis (iii) of R21.5/nearly-ordinary-irreducible-lifting; source issue E11), then ρ comes from a modular form. This is the theorem of the introduction, and Theorem 5.2 (F = ℚ, (5.1), ρ̄^{ss} irreducible and D_p-distinguished, ρ̄^{ss} ≅ ρ̄^{ss}_{π₀} for some π₀). It includes the cases where ρ̄^{ss} is reducible over ℚ(ζ_p), precisely those not covered by Wiles and Diamond.
hypotheses: Skinner–Wiles state it without the extra hypothesis; see E11 for what the printed proof covers

Khare's level-one argument uses this theorem for residually irreducible ρ̄ with ρ̄|_{ℚ(ζ_p)} reducible; there ρ̄ is induced from ℚ(√p*), which is imaginary when p ≡ 3 mod 4, so that branch needs E11 resolved
proofSteps: Hypothesis (ii) of Theorem 5.1 from modularity of ρ̄^{ss}: if p ≠ 3 or ρ̄^{ss}|_{G_{ℚ(√−3)}} is irreducible, Diamond, The refined conjecture of Serre, Theorem 6.4, gives a nearly ordinary π_1 with ρ_{π_1} a χ₂-good lift (SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.6, requested); Skinner–Wiles call the remaining cases obvious.
Apply R21.5/nearly-ordinary-irreducible-lifting with F = ℚ; a cuspidal π of GL₂/ℚ of weight k is a newform (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1).
acceptance: Check that the introduction's (ii)–(v) give (5.1) and D_p-distinguishedness with χ_2 the reduction of the unramified quotient.
The characteristic-zero ρ is assumed irreducible, as in the residually reducible theorems (roadmap check).

nodes.title: The Galois representation of a Hida family over ℚ
nodes.statement: Let p be an odd prime (p ≥ 5 for PadicFamilies' control theorem), N prime to p, Λ = ℤ_p[[1 + pℤ_p]] with fraction field L, T_N Hida's ordinary cuspidal Hecke algebra of tame level N (PadicFamilies L0) and T^new_N its new quotient (the maximal quotient acting faithfully on the ordinary forms new at level N; requested from PadicFamilies L0). (EPW Theorem 2.3.1.) There is a continuous ρ : G_ℚ → GL₂(T^new_N ⊗_Λ L), characterised by (1) ρ unramified outside Np and (2) for ℓ ∤ Np, ρ(Frob_ℓ) has characteristic polynomial X² − T_ℓX + ⟨ℓ⟩ℓ^{−1}; moreover (3) ρ is absolutely irreducible, (4) det ρ is x ↦ ⟨x⟩x^{−1} composed with the cyclotomic character, and (5) the I_p-coinvariants of ρ are free of rank one and Frob_p acts on them by U_p. (Proposition 2.3.2.) For each minimal prime 𝔞 of T^new_N, ρ_𝔞 has tame conductor N. (Proposition 2.3.3.) At a classical height-one prime ℘, for a ρ-stable (T^new_N)_℘-lattice 𝓛 and ℓ ≠ p, 𝓛^{I_ℓ} is free, commutes with ⊗_Λ L and specialises to (𝓛/℘𝓛)^{I_ℓ}, and 𝓛/℘𝓛 carries ρ_{f_℘}. (Theorem 2.3.4.) Each maximal ideal m has a semisimple residual ρ̄_m with the same trace and determinant modulo m and ρ̄_m|_{D_p} ≅ (χ *; 0 ψ) with ψ unramified and ψ(Frob_p) = U_p mod m. (Proposition 2.3.5.) If ρ̄_m is irreducible, ρ_m has a model over (T^new_N)_m, unique up to isomorphism, whose I_p-coinvariants are free of rank one; this gives ρ̄_m its canonical p-stabilisation (Definitions 2.3.6–2.3.7).
hypotheses: the Hecke side (T_N, T^new_N, classical height-one primes, control) is PadicFamilies L0's; this node is the Galois side, which PadicFamilies L4's RS-08 note assigns to this roadmap

R21.3/hida-family-representation covers even-degree totally real F only (Skinner–Wiles' quaternionic towers); this is the classical family over ℚ, from Hida (Invent. Math. 85, 1986, Theorem 2.1) and Greenberg–Stevens (Theorem 2.6) as recalled by EPW
the integral model in Proposition 2.3.5 needs ρ̄_m irreducible; in the residually reducible case only the pseudo-representation is integral
proofSteps: Glue the ρ_{f_℘} over the Zariski-dense classical height-one primes (Hida; Greenberg–Stevens, as cited by EPW), using (3) of Theorem 2.2.2 of EPW (T^new_N ⊗ Λ_℘ is étale over Λ_℘ at classical ℘).
Proposition 2.3.2: compare dim V^{I_ℓ} with dim V(℘)^{I_ℓ} through the conductor formula; the determinant of ρ_𝔞(σ) − 1 on V^{J_ℓ} lies in every classical ℘ of the normalisation, hence vanishes.
Theorem 2.3.4: reduce an integral model over the normalisation, semisimplify and descend.
Proposition 2.3.5: Carayol's theorem (GlobalGaloisDeformations R04.2/carayol-trace-theorem), since the traces lie in (T^new_N)_m and ρ̄_m is irreducible.
acceptance: Check (5) against the ordinarity criterion: at a classical ℘ of weight k, U_p ↦ the unit root α_p of f_℘ and the unramified quotient is the one of PadicHodgeTheory R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion.
Do not claim a GL₂(T^new_N)-valued representation without an irreducibility hypothesis on ρ̄_m.

nodes.title: The exported ordinary newform lies in a Hida family
nodes.statement: Let p ≥ 5 and let f be a newform of weight k ≥ 2 and level N₀ or N₀p (p ∤ N₀) that is ordinary at p (a unit U_p- or T_p-eigenvalue root). Then f, or its unique ordinary p-stabilisation f_α, is the specialisation at a classical height-one prime of a unique primitive component 𝒦 of Hida's ordinary Hecke algebra of tame level N₀ (Hida, Corollary 3.7), and the Galois representation of R21.6/hida-family-galois-representation-over-q specialises there to ρ_{f,λ}. In particular, if ρ is exported by R21.6/exported-ordinary-modularity-over-q (under (ii) ρ|_{I_p} ≅ (∗ ∗; 0 1)), the newform f with ρ ≅ ρ_{f,λ} is ordinary at p and lies in a Hida family whose representation interpolates ρ.
hypotheses: p ≥ 5, the range of PadicFamilies L0's control theorem
ordinarity of f from that of ρ: an unramified quotient of ρ|_{G_{ℚ_p}} forces a unit root (PadicHodgeTheory R06.4/two-dimensional-ordinarity-criterion)
uniqueness of 𝒦 is Hida's Corollary 3.7 (requested from PadicFamilies L0, which owns Hida families)
proofSteps: EPW §2.1 (after Theorem 2.1.2): classical height-one primes of T_N of weight k correspond to Galois-conjugacy classes of p-ordinary normalised eigenforms of tame level N and weight k ≥ 2; hence f_α gives a classical prime ℘_f.
Hida, Corollary 3.7: an ordinary form of weight k ≥ 2 whose primitive form has conductor divisible by N₀ belongs to a unique primitive component.
Specialisation: R21.6/hida-family-galois-representation-over-q (Proposition 2.3.3 and the characterisation by traces).
For the export: ρ|_{I_p} ≅ (∗ ∗; 0 1) gives an unramified quotient, so f is ordinary by the ordinarity criterion.
acceptance: Record multiplicity: a p-old f of level N₀ has two p-stabilisations and only one is ordinary.
k = 2 is allowed for cusp forms (PadicFamilies L0/hida-control-theorem uses k ≥ 2 for cusp forms).

nodes.title: Required example: X₀(11) at p = 5
nodes.statement: Let f be the normalised newform spanning S₂(Γ₀(11)) (X₀(11) has genus 1, so the Hecke algebra T is ℤ). Mazur's Eisenstein ideal 𝔍 ⊆ T (generated by 1 + w and the T_ℓ − 1 − ℓ, ℓ ≠ 11) has T/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/n with n = numerator((11 − 1)/12) = 5 (Proposition II.9.7), so a_ℓ(f) ≡ 1 + ℓ mod 5 for every prime ℓ ≠ 11. Hence: (a) a_5(f) ≡ 1 mod 5, so f is ordinary at 5 (an ordinary weight-two form); (b) ρ̄_{f,5}^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ ω by Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt, a residual split p-distinguished representation: χ = ω is odd and ramified at 5, so χ|_{D_5} ≠ 1; (c) ρ_{f,5} is irreducible and satisfies (i)–(iii) of R21.5/theorem-a-over-q with k = 2, so that theorem applies (and returns f); (d) the reducible 1 ⊕ ε₅ also has residual 1 ⊕ ω and satisfies (i)–(iii) with k = 2 and odd determinant, but is attached to no cuspidal newform, so the irreducibility hypothesis cannot be dropped; (e) p = 5 is in the range of Hida theory, and the ordinary 5-stabilisation f_α of level 55 lies in a Hida family (R21.6/ordinary-newform-lies-in-a-hida-family) whose specialisations at weights k ≡ 2 mod 4 have trivial character; for k > 2 they are 5-old, since a form new at 5 of weight k and trivial character has a_5² = 5^{k−2}, not a unit.
hypotheses: this is the roadmap's 'ordinary weight-two form and its arithmetic specialisations', 'residual p-distinguished split representation' and 'irreducibility of the characteristic-zero representation' checks
the family's residual representation is reducible (Eisenstein), so only its pseudo-representation is integral (R21.6/hida-family-galois-representation-over-q, Proposition 2.3.5 does not apply)
proofSteps: n = numerator(10/12) = 5 and T/𝔍 ≅ ℤ/5 (Mazur Proposition II.9.7); T = ℤ gives the congruences.
a_5 ≡ 1 + 5 ≡ 1: a unit, so f is 5-ordinary; the unramified quotient of ρ_{f,5}|_{G_{ℚ_5}} reduces to 1 and the sub to ω.
ω has order 4 on I_5, so the two residual characters differ on I_5 (checked in the Lean file).
1 ⊕ ε₅ is reducible; cuspidal newforms have irreducible ρ_{f,λ} (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.1).

Weights: the family's character at weight k is ω^{2−k}, trivial exactly when 4 | k − 2; for f new at 5 with trivial character, a_5² = 5^{k−2} (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.4, the Steinberg local factor).
acceptance: Check the numerology in the Lean file: n = 5, a_5 ≡ 1 mod 5, ω nontrivial of order 4, and 5 | a_5² for new forms of weight k > 2.

nodes.title: Required example: when p-distinguishedness holds and when it fails
nodes.statement: (a) Let ρ satisfy (ii) ρ|_{I_p} ≅ (∗ ∗; 0 1) and (iii) det ρ = ψε^{k−1} of R21.5/theorem-a-over-q with ψ unramified at p and p odd. On I_p the residual sub-character is ω^{k−1} and the quotient is 1, so they differ as soon as (p − 1) ∤ (k − 1); for k even this always holds, and hypothesis (i) χ|_{D_p} ≠ 1 is automatic (this is also why Dieulefait–Pacetti's second hypothesis is automatic, source issue E9). (b) The hypothesis fails for the odd character χ_{−23} of ℚ(√−23) at p = 3: 3 splits in ℚ(√−23) because −23 ≡ 1 mod 3, so χ_{−23}|_{D_3} = 1, and R21.5/theorem-a-over-q says nothing about ρ with ρ̄^{ss} ≅ 1 ⊕ χ_{−23}. By (a), an ordinary ρ of this kind with ψ unramified at 3 would need k − 1 even. Whether such ρ exist is not asserted.
hypotheses: (i) is a condition on the residual character only; this node checks it against the other hypotheses
proofSteps: (a) ω^{k−1}|_{I_p} = 1 exactly when (p − 1) | (k − 1); p − 1 is even and k − 1 is odd for k even.
(b) −23 ≡ 1 mod 3 is a square, so 3 splits in ℚ(√−23) and Frob_3 ↦ 1 under χ_{−23}; χ_{−23} is unramified at 3 and odd.
acceptance: Check both parity facts and the splitting of 3 in the Lean file.

requests.need: Definite quaternionic forms over a totally real F of even degree, for D ramified exactly at the infinite places: X(U) = D^×\G^D(A_f)/U finite; H⁰(X(U), R) = H⁰(X(U), ℤ) ⊗ R free of rank #X(U); the Hecke operators [UgU′] (T(ℓ), S(ℓ), T₀(p_v), T₀(p) and the action of G(U_a)) commuting and preserving integrality; the norm-factoring subspace I^D(U); pullback and trace between levels; stabiliser orders c_U(x) with c_{U_a}(x) = 1 for a large; free action after an auxiliary level (Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.5 and Corollary 3.6); and finite-level freeness over 𝒪/πⁿ[Δ_w] for a fixed-point-free action. Also: Eichler's norm theorem for D (every totally positive element of F is a reduced norm) and strong approximation for the norm-one group G^D_1 at a place w where D splits (used in Skinner–Wiles Lemma 3.26).
requests.note: R18.3 owns the quaternionic sets, their Hecke action, change of level and Taylor–Wiles freeness; R21.1 only applies the ordinary projector and passes to the ordinary towers.

requests.need: The Jacquet–Langlands–Shimizu isomorphism S^D(U) = H⁰(X(U), ℂ)/I^D(U) ≅ S₂(U), compatible with all [UgU′], for the definite quaternion algebra over an even-degree totally real field unramified at all finite places.

Adelic Hilbert modular forms M_k(U), S_k(U) of weight k ∈ ℤ[I] with Fourier expansions and Shimura's integrality M_k(n, A) = M_k(n, ℤ) ⊗ A; the Hecke operators T(ℓ), S(ℓ), T₀(p_v); local newform theory (dim V_{π,v}^{U_v} = 1 at unramified v) and Hida's classification of unit T₀(p_v)-eigenlines ([H3, Corollary 2.2]).

Hida's totally real theory on the quaternionic ordinary towers of R21.1 (Skinner–Wiles §3.2): M_∞(U) and M⁺_∞(U) free over Λ′_𝒪 of rank rank_𝒪 eH⁰(X(U⁰_1), 𝒪) × #(G(U)_tors) under the fixed-point-free hypothesis (Proposition 3.3, Hida [H2, Theorem 3.8]); T_∞(U, 𝒪) finite torsion-free over Λ′_𝒪 and semilocal complete (Corollary 3.4); control in all weights (Proposition 3.7, Hida [H2, Corollary 2.5]); density of weight-two algebraic primes on each component (Lemma 3.8, Corollary 3.9); and Wiles' Λ-adic forms ([W2, Theorem 1.4.1]).
requests.note: RS-08: R21.2 imports the cuspidal totally real Hida control from PadicFamilies L5 and keeps only the additional nearly ordinary and Eisenstein statements.

requests.need: The Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function L_p(F, s, χω) with its interpolation of L^{(p)}(F, 1 − n, χω^{1−n}); Hilbert Eisenstein series E_n(φ₁, φ₂) of parallel weight n, spanning a complement of the cusp forms, with constant terms a_i(E_n(1, ψ), 0) = 2^{−d}L(F, 1 − n, ψ)Nm(t_i)^{n/2} (Skinner–Wiles (3.10)); Chai's integral form g with a_i(g, 0) = 2^{−d}Nm(t_i)^{n/2} for large n ≡ 2 mod (p − 1)p^f ([Ch, §4.5], (3.11)); and Wiles' vanishing of Eisenstein combinations with zero constant terms ([W3, Proposition 1.6]). Also the congruences for the Deligne–Ribet p-adic L-function under abelian p-extensions (Skinner–Wiles (4.17), citing [Co], [D-R], [Se]).
Local–global compatibility away from p for the Galois representations of nearly ordinary Hilbert eigenforms: π_v ≅ π_v(ρ_π) for v ∤ p (Skinner–Wiles (3.3), [W2, Theorem 2.1.3]).

For ρ_0 = χ ⊕ 1 on D_i with χ|_{D_i} ≠ 1 and determinant χ̃: the versal local 𝒪-deformation ring R^{(i)} and the versal nearly ordinary ring R^{(i)}_ord (ρ ≅ (χ̃Ψ *; 0 Ψ^{−1}), Ψ ≡ 1), with Skinner–Wiles Lemma 2.2: R^{(i)}_ord ≅ 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_{2d_i+2}]]/(f) if χ|_{D_i} = ω or ω = 1, else 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_{2d_i+1}]] (tangent dimension from local duality); and Corollary 2.3: R^{(i)}_ord is a quotient of R^{(i)} by an ideal generated by d_i + ε_i elements, ε_i = 2 if χ|_{D_i} = ω = χ^{−1}|_{D_i}, 1 if exactly one of χ|_{D_i} = ω, ω = χ^{−1}|_{D_i}, ω = 1 holds in the stated combinations, 0 otherwise.
requests.note: RS-08 gives R21.3 the global deformation rings with L8's local ordinary rings; the residually split p-distinguished case is the one needed here.

requests.need: Mazur's unframed presentation for a Schur residual representation with fixed determinant: R ≅ 𝒪[[x_1, …, x_{g′}]]/(f_1, …, f_{r′}) with g′ = h¹(F_Σ/F, ad⁰ρ̄) and r′ ≤ h²(F_Σ/F, ad⁰ρ̄) ([M, Proposition 2]); R04.3's framed presentation assumes absolute irreducibility.
Tate's global Euler characteristic formula for H^i(F_Σ/F, ad⁰ρ̄) with F totally real and ρ̄ odd, giving h¹ − h² ≥ 2d for ad⁰ρ_c.
Schlessinger's criteria (H1)–(H4) for functors on complete local Noetherian 𝒪-algebras with finite residue field, applied to the functor of pseudo-deformations.

Wiles' Galois representations ρ_π for ordinary Hilbert eigenforms of parallel weight κ ≥ 2 (Skinner–Wiles (3.2), [W2]): ρ_π(z_1) = diag(1, −1), unramified outside 𝔫p, trace ρ_π(Frob_ℓ) = λ(T(ℓ)), det ρ_π(Frob_ℓ) = λ(S(ℓ))Nm(ℓ), det ρ_π(x) = λ(S_x)ε(x), and ρ_π|_{D_i} ≅ (ψ_1 *; 0 ψ_2) with ψ_2(y) = λ(T_y), ψ_2(λ_{𝔭_i}) = λ(T_0(𝔭_i)).

Base change and descent for Hilbert modular forms along solvable totally real extensions (Skinner–Wiles cite [GL]): given a newform f_1 over L with L/F solvable and ρ_{f_1} ≅ ρ|_{G_L} for an irreducible ρ of G_F, a newform f over F with ρ_f|_{G_L} ≅ ρ_{f_1}.

Abstract patching over A = k[[T]] (Skinner–Wiles §5): given rings, trace subrings and modules at levels (N, a) with the axioms (5.1)–(5.11), the level-(a, c) structures take finitely many isomorphism types, nested subsequences give inverse limits, and the patched R_∞ ⊗ K is a power series ring with M_∞ free; the argument works on deformation rings whose residue fields are not finite.
requests.note: RS-08: R21.4 imports abstract module patching from R03.5 and keeps the arithmetic verification (§7).

requests.need: Auslander–Buchsbaum; de Smit–Rubin–Schoof, Criteria for complete intersections (Compositio 1997), Lemma 4.1 and Criterion I (for a surjection R ↠ T of complete local C-algebras finite over a DVR C, with T a reduced complete intersection: R ≅ T iff ℓ_C(H_R/H_R²) ≤ ℓ_C(C/δ(G_T)), and then both are complete intersections).

Chebotarev selection of primes w with Nm(w) ≡ 1 mod p^m and prescribed Frobenius image in the splitting field of ρ mod λ^m together with a cohomology class, for ρ over a characteristic-p DVR A = k[[λ]] (Skinner–Wiles Proposition 6.10).
Wiles' Selmer-group formula #H_Σ(𝒯)/#H*_Σ(𝒯) = h_∞∏_w h_w for finite Galois modules over a totally real field ([W1, Proposition 1.6]; Poitou–Tate with the local Euler characteristic).

Selmer groups with local conditions L_w and their duals L*_w under local duality, and the tangent-space embedding Hom(R, C ⊕ εC/λ^m) ↪ H¹(F_Σ/F, ad ρ/λ^m) with local conditions (Skinner–Wiles (8.8)–(8.10)).
Fontaine's equivalence between ℤ_p-representations of G_{ℚ_p} and étale (φ, Γ)-modules over A_{ℚ_p}, with 𝒪_E-coefficients, used by Berger–Li–Zhu Theorem 4.1 to compare reductions.
Wach modules of crystalline lattices over ℚ_p (Berger 2004, §§II.1, III.4): existence, the bijection T ↦ N(T) with lattices, and N(V)/πN(V) ≅ D_cris(V) for positive V, with 𝒪_E-coefficients.
Dee's theorem: an étale family of (φ, Γ)-modules over ℤ_p[[X]] gives a family of representations (a free ℤ_p[[X]]-module with continuous G_{ℚ_p}-action), specialising at α ∈ 𝔪_E.
Local Galois groups: the unramified quadratic extension ℚ_{p²}, fundamental characters of level 2 and induction from G_{ℚ_{p²}} to G_{ℚ_p}, with the irreducibility criterion for ind(ω₂^j).

Diamond, The refined conjecture of Serre (1995), Theorem 6.4, in the form Skinner–Wiles 2001 use for their Theorem 5.2: for p odd and ρ̄ : G_ℚ → GL₂(F̄_p) irreducible, modular and p-distinguished (ρ̄|_{D_p} ≅ (χ_1 *; 0 χ_2), χ_1 ≠ χ_2), with p ≠ 3 or ρ̄|_{G_{ℚ(√−3)}} irreducible, there is a nearly ordinary cuspidal π_1 of GL₂/ℚ whose p-adic representation is ordinary at p with unramified quotient reducing to χ_2 (a χ₂-good lift).

The versal nearly ordinary deformation ring of a nonsplit ρ₀|_{D_v} ≅ (χ_1 *; 0 χ_2), χ_1 ≠ χ_2, for v | p over a totally real F, with its relative dimension over 𝒪 (Skinner–Wiles 2001 Proposition 2.1 say it is analysed as in their 1999 Corollary 2.3, the split case χ ⊕ 1).

The Hecke side of the classical Hida family over ℚ that R21.6 builds its Galois representation on: Hida's primitive components (Iwasawa modules attached to congruences of cusp forms, Corollary 3.7: an ordinary form of weight k ≥ 2 on Γ₁(N₀p) whose primitive form has conductor divisible by N₀ belongs to a unique primitive component, with d = [𝒦 : ℒ_K] forms at each weight); the correspondence between classical height-one primes of T_N and Galois-conjugacy classes of ordinary eigenforms (EPW Theorem 2.1.2 and after); and the new quotient T^new_N (EPW Definition 2.2.1, Theorem 2.2.2: finite, reduced, torsion-free over Λ, classical primes ↔ forms of tame conductor N, étale over Λ_℘ at classical ℘).

gaps.title: Raynaud's connectedness theorem (Skinner–Wiles Proposition A.1)
gaps.detail: If A is a local Cohen–Macaulay ring of dimension d and I is generated by r ≤ d − 2 elements, Spec(A/I) ∖ {m_A} is connected (Raynaud, Anneaux locaux henséliens, Corollaire 4.2; a form of Grothendieck's connectedness theorem, SGA 2 XIII). Skinner–Wiles cite it without proof. No roadmap stage in the atlas plans it and Mathlib does not have it; it should go to a commutative-algebra owner.

sourceIssues.printed: The source says the map Λ′_𝒪 → Λ_𝒪 specified by the rule 1 + X_j ↦ (1 + T_j)^{p^{r_j}} ε(γ_j^{−p^{r_j}}) respects the Λ′_𝒪-algebra structure on T_∞(U, 𝒪)_m. It claims that Λ_𝒪 is consequently free over Λ′_𝒪 with rank r = Σr_j.
sourceIssues.correction: Λ_𝒪 is a free Λ′_𝒪-module of rank p^{Σ r_j} = ∏_j p^{r_j}.
sourceIssues.reason: In each variable 1 + X ↦ u(1 + T)^{p^r} with u ∈ 1 + pℤ_p, and u(1 + T)^{p^r} − 1 is a unit times a distinguished polynomial of degree p^r, so 𝒪[[T]] is free of rank p^r over 𝒪[[X]] (Weierstrass division); the ranks multiply over the δ_F variables. Lemma 3.10 uses only that Λ_𝒪 is finite free over Λ′_𝒪, and r is not used again.

sourceIssues.locator: §2, the sentence before Lemma 2.2 and Lemma 2.2, p. 191 (Numdam PDF page 8); its uses in the proof of Proposition 4.1, pp. 200 and 202
sourceIssues.printed: The source defines δ⁻_{F′} as the Z_p-rank of the Γ_Σ summand with nontrivial action by Gal(F′/F) ≃ Z/2, and cites [Wal] for δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2. Lemma 2.2 claims dim R_𝒟/q ≤ δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2 whenever q ⊆ R_𝒟 is prime, contains p, and ρ_𝒟 mod q is dihedral with determinant of finite order.
sourceIssues.correction: dim R_𝒟/q ≤ δ⁻_{F′} holds, and δ⁻_{F′} ≤ d/2 holds when F′ is totally real (Waldschmidt applied to the minus part of the units of F′, which has rank d). When F′ is CM, δ⁻_{F′} = d, and the bound dim R_𝒟/q ≤ d/2 fails when every place above p splits in F′. Proposition 4.1 therefore needs, when ρ₀ is dihedral, a separate proof (or an assumption) that the dihedral locus of type 𝒟 with finite-order determinant has dimension at most d/2.
sourceIssues.reason: Affected: Lemma 2.2, and the three steps of the proof of Proposition 4.1 that use it (hence the proofs of Theorems 5.1 and 5.2), when ρ₀ is induced from a quadratic extension F′/F with a complex place. For F′ CM, the global units of F′ have the same rank d − 1 as those of F, so the minus part of the units is finite; the minus part of ∏_{w|p} 𝒪_{F′,w}^× has ℤ_p-rank d, and class field theory gives δ⁻_{F′} = d > d/2. The lemma's conclusion then fails: if every v | p splits in F′ and ℳ = ∅, Ind_{F′}^F(ψ̃₀ψ⁻), with ψ⁻ the universal character of the free part of the minus quotient of Γ_Σ, is a deformation of type 𝒟 over k[[Γ⁻]] (at each v_i it is Ψ|_{D_w} ⊕ Ψ|_{D_w̄}, nearly ordinary with the χ^{(i)}_1-part as sub). Its determinant has finite order, and its trace ring has dimension d. Such ρ₀ satisfy (2.1): for example ρ̄_{E,p}|_{G_F} for an elliptic curve E with complex multiplication by K, p ≥ 5 split in K, and a totally real F of even degree, linearly disjoint from K(E[p]), over which ρ̄_{E,p} is unramified outside p. The proof of Proposition 4.1 uses the d/2 bound three times: that ρ₁ = ρ^mod mod Q is not dihedral (step one, p. 200); that ρ mod Q₁ is not dihedral because dim Q₁ > 1 + d/2 (step three, p. 200); and that ρ mod Q₂ is not dihedral because dim Q₂ ≥ d/2 + 1 (general case, p. 202). Theorem 5.1 passes to L with ρ₀ = ρ̄^{ss}|_{G_L}, and F′L is CM when F′ is. Not examined: whether Theorems 5.1 and 5.2 fail in these cases, which are partly covered by other lifting theorems when ρ̄|_{F(ζ_p)} is irreducible. When the places above p do not split in F′, the nearly ordinary condition forces Ψ⁻ to have finite order on their decomposition groups, which should cut the dihedral locus down; the paper does not make this argument.

sourceIssues.locator: §4, the last paragraph of the proof of Proposition 4.1, p. 202 (Numdam PDF page 19); the hypotheses (4.1), p. 198
sourceIssues.printed: The source uses Proposition 2.1 to bound the dimension of Q₂ below by d − 7·#Σ − 1, and combines this with (4.1) to claim a lower bound of d/2 + 1.
sourceIssues.correction: (4.1) bounds only #ℳ₀. The step needs d/2 > 2 + 2t + 7·#(Σ ∖ 𝒫) (implied by d/2 > 2 + 7·#Σ), which should be added to the hypotheses of Proposition 4.1. Theorem 5.1 chooses L with d_L/2 > 2 + 7·#Σ_L, so its proof is unaffected.
sourceIssues.reason: Affected: the proof of Proposition 4.1 for data 𝒟 with Σ larger than Σ₀; not the proof of Theorem 5.1, which imposes the needed bound. Proposition 2.1 gives every minimal prime Q of R_𝒟 dimension at least 1 + d + δ_F − 2t − 3#ℳ, and I₂ is generated by 1 + 4#(Σ ∖ 𝒫) + δ_F elements, so dim Q₂ ≥ d − 2t − 3#ℳ − 4#(Σ ∖ 𝒫). For Σ = Σ₀ this exceeds d/2 + 1 by (4.1)(i), but not in general: d = 40, t = 1 and ℳ₀ = ∅ satisfy (4.1)(i), while #Σ = 4 gives d − 7#Σ − 1 = 11 < 21 = d/2 + 1 (checked in the suggested Lean file). The corresponding good-pair condition of Skinner–Wiles 1999 involves #Σ; (4.1) here depends only on (F, ρ₀).
